title: The Curve Is the Material — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of The Curve Is the Material's rich face, its first round, a Sketch and still a proposal: one walk that starts on the flat harmonic line and ends on a measurement of the section's distinction, between morphing a stiff string's one number and blending its two end curves point by point. I grow when the page is enriched again, toward the function picker its forward vector asks for; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The piece measures how far the curve blend strays, and for the section's own pair it is not far. Blended point by point in cents, as frames of Wavetable B are scanned, 0.001 → 0.003 is never one string between its ends (at t = 0.5 partial 1 reads B = 0.00200, partial 24 reads 0.00186), but its worst partial stays within 1.56 ¢ of a real string at 16 partials, 4.03 ¢ at 24 and 12.3 ¢ at 64, which is 0.5–0.7 % of the stretch it carries (fit with B and f₀ both free). The gap grows as the ends move apart and the partials go higher: 0.0002 → 0.004 gives 15.7 ¢ at 24 partials and 65.3 ¢ at 64; 0.001 → 0.1 gives 149 ¢. Suggest the first paragraph say so: the blend leaves the family by an amount set by how far apart the frames are and how many partials there are. For nearby strings it is a few cents, so a Wavetable B with closely spaced frames already morphs almost as a string would.

The third paragraph sets function-type interpolation ("the weighted sum of two real physical models") against arbitrary curve blending. But a weighted sum taken partial by partial is the same operation as the curve blend the first paragraph warns about. The piece shows that what decides whether a blend stays near a physical model is its two ends, not the blending: the same point-by-point blend stays within 4 ¢ of a string between 0.001 and 0.003 and is 149 ¢ off between 0.001 and 0.1. So "qualitatively different from arbitrary curve blending" holds because of the ends it picks (two physical models instead of any two drawn curves), not because it takes a different path. That is reasoning from the piece; a string-to-Bessel blend was not measured.

offers.section: Design Implication: Function Library Over Freehand Curve
offers.what: Calculated on the coefficient formula B = π³·E·d⁴/(64·T·L²), not tested by a piece. "B ≈ 0.004 (heavy piano bass string)" seems to have the piano upside down: B is lowest in the wound bass and highest in the short treble strings. It is of order 10⁻⁴ mid-keyboard and 10⁻² at the top (Acta Acustica 2021, doi 10.1051/aacus/2021002), and the Piano String Inharmonicity May proof gives 0.0001 (bass) to 0.004 (treble). A plain steel string of 0.775 mm, 51 mm long, at 700 N (assumed dimensions, close to C8) gives B = 0.019. So "B > 0.01: no real material" is crossed by the top of a piano.

Calculated, not tested by a piece. "Hyper-stiff strings with B = 0.1 produce inharmonic spectra nothing physical ever generates": by the coefficient formula, a 1.5 mm steel wire 10 cm long at 500 N (283 MPa, well inside music wire's strength) has B = 0.098 and sounds near 950 Hz. As B·n² grows, the formula's partials go as n², the series of a bar pinned at both ends (Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis already plays that string-to-bar morph). So the hyper-stiff string is a short, thick, tight wire on its way to a bar, a real object. The section's point that the constraint is generative stands; the 'nothing physical' clause doesn't.

pieces.title: two ways to morph a string · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **Does blending the curves leave the family, and by how much?** The flat harmonic line, bowed by one number B; then a way to read the stiffness back off every partial, where a real string reads one B from all of them; then the section's two strings, 0.001 and 0.003, morphed by the number; then the same two blended partial by partial, where the reading tilts from the average at partial 1 toward the geometric mean at the top; and last the test, every point of both morphs measured against the nearest real string. The number's morph stays a string. The blend leaves the family, but between the section's own pair only by about 4 ¢ at 24 partials; the gap opens as the strings move apart and the partials go higher. See the offers on this section.
